Lemma
[The Inverse of an Isometry]

↗ def:isometry

If $\varphi :(M,g)\to (\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ is an isometry, then $\varphi ^{-1}$ is an isometry in the opposite direction.
Proof

↗ def:isometry ↗ def:metric-preserving \sketch For $q=\varphi (p)$, differentiate $\varphi \circ \varphi ^{-1}=\operatorname {id}$ to obtain $d\varphi _p\circ d(\varphi ^{-1})_q=\operatorname {id}$. Applying $\varphi ^*\widetilde g=g$ to $d(\varphi ^{-1})_qv,d(\varphi ^{-1})_qw$ gives

\[ g_p(d(\varphi ^{-1})_qv,d(\varphi ^{-1})_qw)=\widetilde g_q(v,w), \]

so $(\varphi ^{-1})^*g=\widetilde g$.

□
